points.description: Identifies that the recursive step is defined incorrectly (e.g. the recursive call does not move closer to the base case, or the step is wrong), so the recursion never terminates. Equivalent wording earns the mark.
Identifies that the base case is missing or not included, so the recursion has no point at which it stops. Equivalent wording earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks for naming both causes: a faulty recursive step and a missing base case. Each cause is worth 2.5 marks and is all-or-nothing. Answers that give only one cause get 2.5 marks. Equivalent wording and other correct explanations of the same two causes are accepted.
